user.title: Energy Price Graph
user.description: Adds a dynamic electricity price graph to the built-in Energy dashboard. The price sensors are read from your energy settings (Electricity grid → costs / compensation). You can change the options afterwards via Configure. Refresh your browser once after setup.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Energy Price Graph is already set up.

init.title: Energy Price Graph options
init.description: Changes apply the next time you open the Energy dashboard.

graph.name: Price graph
graph.description: How the price graph looks and on which tabs it is shown.

data.views: Show the price graph on tabs

data_description.period: Auto (fine) shows every price step (5-minute data, so quarter-hour prices change exactly at :00, :15, :30 and :45) for periods up to a week within the recorder history, and hourly or daily averages for longer periods. Auto uses hourly averages for a day. 5-minute data is kept as long as your recorder keeps history (purge_keep_days, default 10 days).
data_description.line_style: Straight connects the points directly. Stepped shows the exact price per period. Smooth draws a rounded curve.
data_description.views: Tabs of the Energy dashboard where the electricity price graph is shown.
data_description.show_export: Adds a second line when the export price is a different sensor than the import price.
data_description.minmax: Also draws the lowest and highest price within each period.

markers.name: Markers in the graph
markers.description: Extra lines and highlighted areas in the price graph.

data.show_now_line: Show a line at the current time
data.show_average_line: Show the average price as a line
data.cheapest_hours: Highlight the cheapest hours per day

data_description.show_now_line: Vertical dashed line at the current time when the selected period includes now.
data_description.show_average_line: Horizontal dotted line at the average import price of the period shown (including upcoming prices).
data_description.cheapest_hours: Shades the N cheapest hours of each day (0 = off), for example to plan the washing machine or charging. Only for days of which (almost) all prices are known, so with a forecast also today and tomorrow.
data_description.highlight_negative: Shades the area below zero and draws a zero line when the price is negative.

current.name: Current price
current.description: Chips with the current price in the header of the graph.

data_description.show_current: Small chips in the card header with the current price.
data_description.show_price_colors: Green when the current price is favourable compared to today's average price (the whole day when a forecast is available, otherwise the prices so far today) (low for import and gas, high for export), orange around the average, red when unfavourable.
data_description.price_color_threshold: How far the price may differ from today's average and still count as average (orange). Measured against the average price or, when prices are close to zero, against half of today's price range.

average.name: Average price
average.description: Card below Energy distribution on the Electricity tab.

data.import_surcharge: Surcharge on market import price (per kWh)
data.export_surcharge: Surcharge on market export price (per kWh)

data_description.show_average: Card below Energy distribution on the Electricity tab with your average import and export price for the selected period, next to the average market price.
data_description.show_savings: Shows how much better or worse you did than the market average, in your currency, for import and export separately and in total.
data_description.show_timing: Share of your import in the cheapest and most expensive quarter of the hours of each day (for periods up to 35 days). With evenly spread use both are about 25 %.
data_description.import_surcharge: Added to the average of the import price sensor, for example energy tax and your supplier's markup, when your costs include them but the price sensor does not. 0 = none.
data_description.export_surcharge: Added to the average of the export price sensor (can be negative, for example a feed-in fee). 0 = none.

data.gas_views: Show the gas price graph on tabs

data_description.show_gas: Price graph using the gas price sensor from your energy settings.
data_description.gas_views: Tabs of the Energy dashboard where the gas price graph is shown.

forecast.name: Forecast (upcoming prices)
forecast.description: Upcoming prices are drawn as a dashed line; open tomorrow in the date picker to see tomorrow. They are read from the attributes of a sensor (for example Nord Pool, ENTSO-e, Zonneplan or Frank Energie) or, for Nord Pool, Tibber, EnergyZero and easyEnergy in Home Assistant, from the action of the integration.

data_description.forecast_auto: When no forecast sensor is chosen below, look for upcoming prices on the price sensor itself (attributes or integration action).
data_description.forecast_import_entity: Leave empty to use the price sensor itself (see above) or for no forecast line.
data_description.forecast_export_entity: Leave empty to use the price sensor itself (see above) or for no forecast line.
data_description.forecast_gas_entity: Leave empty to use the price sensor itself (see above) or for no forecast line.
data_description.forecast_attribute: Only read this attribute, for example raw_tomorrow or prices. Leave empty to search all attributes.
data_description.forecast_value_key: Name of the field with the price in each item, for example value or price_incl_vat. Leave empty to detect it.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Overrides for sensors, title and names.

data_description.title: Leave empty for the default title.
data_description.import_entity: Leave empty to use the sensor from your energy settings.
data_description.export_entity: Leave empty to use the sensor from your energy settings.
data_description.gas_entity: Leave empty to use the sensor from your energy settings.

error.no_gas_views: Select at least one tab for the gas price graph, or turn the gas price off.

import_paid_month.name: Average import price paid this month

import_market_month.name: Average market import price this month

export_paid_month.name: Average export price received this month

export_market_month.name: Average market export price this month

frontend_not_active.title: The price graph could not be added to the Energy dashboard

no_price_sensor.title: No price sensor for the price graph
no_price_sensor.description: Energy Price Graph found no electricity price sensor in your energy settings, so no price graph is shown. Set one in Settings → Dashboards → Energy → Electricity grid (costs: "Use an entity with current price"), or choose a sensor in the Advanced section of the integration options. With a fixed price you can ignore this message: the average price card still works.
